messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Below is a concise guide covering the most important aspects of Texas traffic laws as of 2024. For detailed statutory text you’ll want to consult the **Texas Transportation Code** and the *Official Guide to Texas Traffic Laws* published annually by the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV). --- ### 1️⃣ General Road‑Use Rules | Rule | Key Points | |------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• In rural areas, “speed limit” defaults to 55 mph if no sign posted.
• On highways, speed limits range from 45–75 mph depending on road type. | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years old must use approved child safety seats/booster chairs. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield at stop signs, uncontrolled intersections, crosswalks, railroad crossings, and when turning into a lane occupied by another vehicle. | | **Headlights** | • Must be used between sunset and sunrise, during rain/snow, fog, or low visibility conditions. | --- ### 2️⃣ Common Violations & Penalties | Violation | Typical Fine / Consequence | Notes | |-----------|-----------------------------|-------| | Speeding (up to 20 % over) | $100–$300 fine + demerit points | Points accumulate toward license suspension after 12 months. | | Reckless Driving | Up to $500 fine + possible jail time up to 30 days | Requires proof of endangerment. | | DUI/DWI | Minimum $400 fine + mandatory alcohol education program; potential license revocation | First offense may result in 90-day license suspension. | | Texting While Driving | $200 fine + 5 demerits | Applies to all drivers regardless of age. | | Failure to Stop at Red Light | $150 fine + 5 demerits | If collision occurs, additional liability applies. | | Improper Lane Change | $50–$250 fine | Depends on severity and resulting damage. | *(All fines listed above are approximate and can vary based on county courts.)* --- ### 3️⃣ Special Provisions | Provision | Details | |----------|---------| | **School Bus Law** | Drivers must yield to school buses stopping to pick up/drop off children. Failure results in a $350 fine plus 10 demerits. | | **Highway Patrol Authority** | Officers have expanded powers to enforce traffic laws, including issuing citations without a warrant. | | **Red-Light Cameras** | Operated only in specific counties (e.g., Dallas County); tickets issued via mail. | | **Commercial Vehicle Regulations** | Additional weight restrictions, hours-of-service rules, and electronic logging device requirements. | --- ### 4️⃣ How to Check Your Status | Tool | What It Shows | |-----|---------------| | **TX DMV Online License Lookup** | Current status, suspensions, demerit point balance. | | **County Court Records Portal** | Access to your citation history and court dates. | | **Texas Courts App** | Mobile app for checking case docket numbers and hearing schedules. | --- ### 5️⃣ Resources & Where to Find More Info | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | **Texas Transportation Code** | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/?link=TR | | **TxDMV Official Website – Driver’s Handbook** | https://www.txdmv.gov/sites/default/files/documents/TexasDriverHandbook.pdf | | **Texas Department of Public Safety – Traffic Enforcement Division** | https://dps.texas.gov/divisions/public-safety/traffic-enforcement | | **Legal Aid Center – Texas** | https://lawhelp.txstate.edu/legal-aid-center.html | | **State Bar Association – Lawyer Referral Service** | https://www.texasbar.com/LawyerReferralService | --- #### Quick Tips for Staying Compliant 1. **Always obey posted signage—especially in construction zones.** 2. **Keep your driver's license active:** renew before expiration and address any pending infractions promptly. 3. **If cited, consider attending a defensive-driving course**—many jurisdictions offer reduced fines or demerit-point reductions upon completion. 4. **For commercial operators, stay current on Hours-of-Service (HOS) logs**—failure can lead to hefty penalties and loss of operating authority. Feel free to let me know if you need deeper dives into any specific area (e.g., DUI procedures, commercial trucking regulations, or how to contest a ticket)!
message.reasoning:
The user wants information on traffic laws in Texas. They didn't ask specifically for searching lawsuits; they want general info. We can provide an overview or direct them to resources.

We should respond with relevant details: major statutes (Texas Transportation Code), common violations, penalties, etc. Also mention where to find official sources like TxDOT website, Texas Department of Public Safety, and legal references. Provide some key points: speeding limits, seat belt law, DUI regulations, texting while driving, red light cameras, etc. Possibly include links.

No tool needed.
